claims.text: In the model at open-source.sgit.ai the technology is not the moat; customers stay for the service, the quality and the trust, and the company sells trust, not access to a repository.
claims.quote: we are selling trust, not access to a repository

claims.text: In an open source company every corner of the triangle, founders, customers and investors, has an exit that takes the technology with it, and each exit has a condition.
claims.quote: In an open source company every corner has an exit, and the exit takes the technology with it.

claims.text: Robles and González-Barahona studied 220 significant forks: only 7, about 3%, merged back, 44% carried on side by side and in 30% the original was discontinued.
claims.quote: Only 7 of the 220, about 3%, merged back with the original.

claims.text: Forking is considered a last resort even though it is built into free software; it is a serious, expensive and usually permanent decision.
claims.quote: is considered as a last resort

claims.text: LibreOffice followed Oracle's purchase of Sun; by the Document Foundation's count, in 2019 LibreOffice had over 15,000 code commits while OpenOffice had 595.
claims.quote: In 2019, LibreOffice had over 15,000 code commits, while OpenOffice had only 595.

claims.text: io.js forked Node.js over governance in December 2014 and merged back in Node.js 4.0 in September 2015: the fork fixed the problem, then dissolved.
claims.quote: the fork fixed the problem, then dissolved

claims.text: After HashiCorp moved Terraform to the Business Source License, OpenTofu launched under the Linux Foundation with a commitment of at least 18 full-time developers for five years.
claims.quote: a starting commitment of a minimum of 18 full-time developers over at least the next five years

value.unit: full-time developers pledged for five years

claims.text: Eight days after Redis left its open source licence, the Linux Foundation launched Valkey, backed by AWS, Google Cloud, Oracle, Ericsson and Snap.
claims.quote: Eight days later, on 28 March, the Linux Foundation launched Valkey, backed by AWS, Google Cloud, Oracle, Ericsson and Snap.

claims.text: The common thread in the forks that took hold is not that the original stopped innovating but that it stopped doing what its users needed.
claims.quote: It is that it stopped doing what its users needed

claims.text: MariaDB was created in 2009 to protect MySQL from its new owners; Oracle kept MySQL going, and in October 2026 MySQL is second in the DB-Engines ranking and MariaDB thirteenth.
claims.quote: MySQL is second in the DB-Engines ranking, with MariaDB thirteenth

claims.text: Commits to MySQL's trunk fell from about 8,900 in 2019 to about 2,800 in 2025, a fall of roughly two thirds, measured by this site from a clone.
claims.quote: They fell from about 8,900 in 2019 to about 2,800 in 2025.

value.unit: commits a year to mysql-server trunk, 2025 against 2019

claims.text: If the argument is right, this is when MariaDB's share should start to grow; that is a prediction and it can be checked.
claims.quote: If the argument here is right, this is when MariaDB's share should start to grow. That is a prediction, and it can be checked.

claims.text: The real defence is execution, and in the generative AI era speed: the moat is a rate, not a wall, and a competitor who forks today gets your position, not your velocity.
claims.quote: the moat is a rate, not a wall: a competitor who forks today gets your position, not your velocity

claims.text: The stronger version of the self-selecting investor is the one who needs the project to succeed because their own business depends on it, as Valkey's and OpenTofu's backers did.
claims.quote: It is the investor who needs the project to succeed, because their own business depends on it.

claims.text: Startups backed by corporate venture capital produced 26.9% more patents in the three years before IPO than those backed by independent VCs, with 17.6% more citations.
claims.quote: produced 26.9% more patents in the three years before their IPO

value.unit: percent more patents before IPO with corporate venture backing

claims.text: Committed investors may well get the better return too, because they back what they understand and will not abandon it at the first bad quarter; there is no data for that.
claims.quote: My guess is that they may well get the better return too

claims.text: Frank Karlitschek left ownCloud in April 2016 and Nextcloud launched on a fork on 2 June; it turned profitable by the end of 2016 and ran ten years without outside investment.
claims.quote: turned profitable by the end of 2016

claims.text: The founder's exit depends on the contract: venture investors usually ask for a non-compete, and the NVCA's model agreement provides for one from key employees.
claims.quote: those clauses exist to make it expensive for a founder to walk away

claims.text: A founder who wants the fork to protect them should refuse a broad non-compete and offer narrower promises: confidentiality, no poaching for a while, no use of the brand.
claims.quote: A founder who wants the fork to protect them, not only their investors, should refuse a broad non-compete, and offer narrower promises instead

claims.text: Open code is necessary but not enough for the customers' corner; their real exit is their data in an open format, movable to whoever serves the same code better at a cost close to zero.
claims.quote: The customer's real exit is their data, in an open format, that they can take to whoever serves the same code better, at a cost close to zero.

claims.text: A component many companies depend on can move to a neutral home: Google donated Kubernetes to the newly formed CNCF as it reached version 1.0 in July 2015.
claims.quote: Google donated Kubernetes to the newly formed Cloud Native Computing Foundation as it reached version 1.0 in July 2015

claims.text: Google wanted Kubernetes to become the standard way to run software on any cloud, its rivals' included, and a neutral home was how to get rivals to adopt it.
claims.quote: In my reading, it wanted Kubernetes to become the standard way to run software on any cloud

claims.text: Open source lets the explorers take the code and carry on elsewhere, so the technology does not die because the company that started it has become a town planner.
claims.quote: The technology does not die because the company that started it has moved on to a different stage of life.

claims.text: You can be out-served while still executing: Redis and Elastic changed licences because cloud providers sold their healthy code, and open source does not protect against a larger service provider.
claims.quote: Open source protects the corners of the triangle from each other; it does not protect the company from a larger service provider.

claims.text: Licence changes can reverse: Elastic added an open source licence again in 2024 and Redis in 2025, which fits the triangle, as the credible threat of a fork pushed the originals back towards openness.
claims.quote: the credible threat of the fork pushed the original back towards openness

claims.text: Forks are expensive, so setting up next door is a credible threat for investors who depend on the technology, not for a small angel.
claims.quote: The protection is strongest for the investors who need it most.

claims.text: Every catalogued relicensing between 2018 and 2024 was by a single corporate copyright holder; the fork protects what is released, and a single holder can still change the terms going forward.
claims.quote: The fork protects what has already been released; a single holder can still change the terms going forward.

claims.text: No study tests the triangle as a whole; the cases fit the argument but are not a controlled comparison.
claims.quote: No study tests the triangle as a whole.

claims.text: The fork cases are famous ones; successful forks get written about and failed ones mostly do not, which is survivorship bias in its own right.
claims.quote: The fork cases are famous ones.

claims.text: Higher returns for committed investors are a guess, not a finding; no data shows open source companies return more to investors.
claims.quote: Higher returns are a guess, not a finding.

claims.text: The patent figures measure innovation, not financial return, and corporate investors bring their own conflicts.
claims.quote: The patent figures measure innovation, not financial return.

claims.text: Commit counts are a rough measure; MySQL's fall is real in the repository, but whether it means less work or work done elsewhere the count cannot say.
claims.quote: Commit counts are a rough measure.

claims.text: This is not legal advice: non-compete law differs by country and state, and by whether the promise is given as an employee or as a shareholder.
claims.quote: Non-compete law differs by country and state, and by whether the promise is given as an employee or as a shareholder.

claims.text: Not every component should be moved to a foundation; some town-planner work belongs inside the company that runs it.
claims.quote: Not that every component should be moved to a foundation.

claims.text: The owner has a stake: his companies run on open source and this model suits them.
claims.quote: My companies run on open source, and this model suits them.
